title: Debt contract reconciliation and faithful fixtures
objective: Freeze the canonical-versus-legacy debt contract and prove it against faithful original-incident fixtures before any new remediation writer is introduced.

phases.title: Faithful failure baseline

tasks.title: Create the faithful debt compatibility corpus
tasks.description: Add a minimized, non-secret golden corpus covering exact canonical debt, legacy-compatible debt, the live model-catalog D1 shape, the Sprint 1 checkpoint variant without note, the Sprint 2 checkpoint variant with note, and structurally unsupported debt. Record expected classification, canonical projection where defined, decisive legacy keys, and field-level diagnostics.
tasks.context: ADR-0001 and ADR-0005 govern this task. Preserve the original string origin and missing priority/targetSprint/note variants as sentinel facts; do not simplify them into an otherwise canonical debt. The original Aliva checkout is read-only and may only be inspected or copied to a temporary directory. The fixture must not contain project secrets or unrelated application data.
acceptance_criteria: The corpus contains canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required live D1, Sprint 1 historical, Sprint 2 historical, and unsupported cases with explicit expected outcomes.

Sentinel assertions fail if the live D1 origin stops being a string, if priority or targetSprint appears, if the Sprint 1 note appears, or if legacy detail/resolution/addedSprint keys are silently removed.
The fixture checker proves the corpus is minimized, contains no absolute local paths, and is deterministic JSON.
A mutation test changing any decisive expected classification or legacy shape causes the checker to exit non-zero.

tasks.title: Lock the debt compatibility behavior matrix
tasks.description: Build a focused contract harness over the golden corpus that defines the four raw-input outcomes, exact canonical values for readable inputs, field-specific issues for remediable inputs, and unsupported failure behavior without relying on the current SprintFile validator.
tasks.context: This is the executable statement of ADR-0001. Compatibility is not canonicality. Missing fields that Lens can normalize are legacy-compatible; a present wrong type such as string origin is remediation-required; malformed identity or status is unsupported. Do not implement the classifier inside the test or permit snapshots to pass by deleting assertions.
acceptance_criteria: The harness asserts canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported as four distinct outcomes.
Readable inputs have exact expected canonical projections, including Lens-compatible defaults, while invalid present values retain exact field diagnostics.
The focused command is registered in package.json and exits non-zero when production classification behavior is missing or differs from the corpus.
The harness never writes a Kyro scope or the Lens checkout.

evidence.summary: Added scripts/check-debt-contract.mjs, a focused harness that holds production classification to the golden corpus: four distinct outcomes, exact canonical projection in canonical key order for readable inputs, identity with the Lens projection, and exact field diagnostics for remediable ones. It never implements the classifier and never writes: fs mutators are stubbed to throw and watched sprint.json digests are compared before and after. Refined the corpus to the real Lens contract read from kyro-lens/src/data/parse.ts:570 — absent fields are legacy-compatible and normalizable (priority medium, targetSprint null, note composed from Source/Resolution/Disposition, origin from the sprint number), a present wrong-typed value such as the D1 string origin is remediation-required, and unusable id/title/status is unsupported. Corpus grew to 8 cases (added unsupported-missing-id and unsupported-bad-status for S4) and each case now records context.sprintNumber and the expected Lens accept/projection/failure.

phases.title: Contract implementation
phases.objective: Separate raw compatibility assessment from exact canonical debt validation and expose actionable Doctor behavior.

tasks.title: Implement the raw debt assessment contract
tasks.description: Introduce a pure typed debt-input assessment that returns canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, or unsupported with deterministic field issues and an exact canonical projection only when the raw input is safely readable.
tasks.context: Apply ADR-0001 and the shared-debt-vectors convention. The assessment must consume unknown safely, expose no any payload, reject present invalid types, and keep evidence separate from operator authority. This task defines reading/classification only; it must not add a remediation operation or mutate state.
acceptance_criteria: The exported result is a closed discriminated union with exactly canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported states.
Canonical and legacy-compatible results contain exact seven-field canonical projections; remediation-required and unsupported results do not fabricate a trusted projection.
Every issue names a stable field path and reason, and unknown or malformed input fails without throwing an unhandled exception.
All golden cases and mutations pass the production-backed focused harness with strict TypeScript compilation.

evidence.summary: Implemented src/cli/artifacts/debt-contract.ts: assessRawDebt(unknown, {sprintNumber}) is pure, total and non-throwing, returning a closed discriminated union over canonical, legacy_compatible, remediation_required and unsupported. Unusable identity or status short-circuits to unsupported; a present wrong-typed value blocks and yields canonical:null; absence is compatible and normalizable, so readable inputs get an exact seven-field projection in canonical key order using the same defaults Lens applies. REVIEW FIX (R1 parity gap): 'present and wrong' now spans the typed legacy vocabulary, not only canonical keys. A non-string severity, source, resolution or disposition is blocking (LEGACY_VALUE_NOT_STRING), and an unmapped severity string is blocking (SEVERITY_NOT_RECOGNIZED) exactly while it is the sole source of a priority — with an explicit priority present the compatibility reader ignores it, and so does the classification. detail and addedSprint stay outside the vocabulary and constrain nothing. Every diagnostic names a stable field path, code, severity and authority: evidence-backed suggestions carry their evidence, operator judgments carry none (ADR-0004).
validation: npm run typecheck (strict) -> 0; npm run check (aggregate) -> exit 0

12 legacy-field vectors probed against the real Lens parser and against dist: identical accept/reject and identical projections, including severity blocker->critical, MAJOR->high, and unmapped severity ignored when priority is present

evidence.notes: The review reported an unmapped severity string as an unconditional Lens rejection. Probing the real parser refined it: parse.ts guards that check with priority === undefined, so severity 'unknown' with a valid priority is accepted. Both branches are now golden vectors (legacy-severity-unrecognized and legacy-severity-unrecognized-with-priority) so the exact guard cannot drift silently.

tasks.title: Separate exact canonical validation from compatibility reading
tasks.description: Refactor the debt validation boundary so new writes and canonical post-states require exactly the seven canonical keys while raw diagnostic readers can assess legacy input without weakening mutating commands or accepting hybrid output.
tasks.context: ADR-0001 and ADR-0004 apply. New debt writes remain strict and exact. Legacy-only keys must never become acceptable canonical output merely because a reader recognizes them. Existing commands that call validateSprintFile must be inventoried so the refactor does not make mutation permissive or recovery unreachable.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical debt validation requires exactly id, title, origin, priority, status, targetSprint, and note with their existing value constraints.
kyro debt add still emits exact canonical debt, and add/resolve/escalate continue refusing a scope whose live debt is not canonical without writes.
Legacy compatibility assessment remains available to read-only diagnostic and future remediation preparation paths without being used as write authorization.
Extra legacy keys, missing canonical keys, invalid literals, and wrong types each have regression coverage at the correct boundary.

evidence.summary: Split the debt validation boundary. schema.ts now exposes CANONICAL_DEBT_KEY_VALUES and DEBT_VALIDATION_MODE; validateDebtItem rejects any key outside the seven canonical ones in exact mode, and validateSprintFile takes an optional { debt } mode defaulting to exact so every write path stays strict. Compatible mode keeps the previous required-field checks and tolerates legacy-only keys, so readers and future remediation preparation can still parse a legacy scope. debt.ts refuses add/resolve/escalate on a drifted scope before any write and now names what the live debt actually is via a read-only assessRawDebt reading, with the remedy stating explicitly that the reading is a diagnostic, not authorization. Inventoried all validateSprintFile callers: mutating commands, remediation transactions and certification plans keep the exact default; checkpointSchemaIssues stays exact by design because it reports schema currency of historical images separately from integrity, which never gates their commitment.

tasks.title: Report debt compatibility truthfully in Doctor
tasks.description: Wire the assessment contract into artifact Doctor so canonical live debt passes, legacy-compatible live debt is visibly non-canonical, remediation-required debt fails with actionable paths, unsupported debt fails closed, and historical schema notes never skip checkpoint artifact integrity verification.
tasks.context: The history-immutability convention and ADR-0001 govern this task. A legacy-compatible state may be readable but must not be labeled canonical. A string origin must remain remediation-required. Historical checkpoint schema differences are notes subordinate to commitment, snapshot, and narrative integrity; never reintroduce an early return that launders tampering. Do not reference unshipped CLI verbs in user-facing remedies.
acceptance_criteria: Doctor emits distinct canonical, legacy-compatible, remediation-required, and unsupported diagnostics with deterministic exit behavior and exact field paths.
The faithful live D1 case fails as remediation-required for its present invalid origin and also reports missing canonical fields without claiming Lens cannot read those omissions.
Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 historical variants retain schema notes while intact snapshot/narrative commitments pass and any byte tampering still exits non-zero.
Mutation tests that restore strict-input/output conflation or historical early-return behavior fail with specific assertions.

evidence.summary: Doctor now reports the debt contract on its own check (scope/debt-contract), emitted before and independently of generic shape drift so it survives the early return: canonical passes, legacy-compatible warns as readable-but-not-canonical, remediation-required fails naming each present invalid field path, and unsupported fails closed. Remediation-required output also lists absent canonical fields explicitly as 'absent, readable by default, needs an explicit value', so an omission is never presented as unreadable while an operator decision is still required. No unshipped CLI verb appears in any remedy: they describe what must happen, not a command that does not exist yet.

phases.title: Cross-repository and runtime proof
phases.objective: Prove that the frozen contract matches Lens observable behavior and survives build and runtime projection.

tasks.title: Verify the golden debt corpus against Lens
tasks.description: Add an explicit cross-repository conformance command that runs the golden raw-debt cases through the current Lens parser and compares parse success, rejection paths, and canonical projections with the Kyro contract without modifying Lens.
tasks.context: Use the existing KYRO_LENS_ROOT opt-in pattern and the aliva-readonly-probe convention. Lens remains an independent consumer: the check must execute Lens behavior rather than duplicate normalizeDebt inside Kyro. This Sprint freezes observable parity; Lens protocol/UI changes remain Sprint 4 work.
acceptance_criteria: With KYRO_LENS_ROOT pointing to the Lens checkout, canonical and legacy-compatible cases parse to the exact expected canonical values and invalid present types are rejected at the expected path.
The command fails clearly when Lens is absent, the corpus is stale, Lens behavior diverges, or a case is skipped.
The command performs no writes in Lens and leaves the original Aliva checkout untouched.
A mutation to either the Kyro expected projection or Lens-observable result makes conformance exit non-zero.

evidence.summary: Added scripts/check-lens-debt-contract.mjs plus check:lens-debt-contract: an opt-in cross-repository gate that runs every golden case through the real Lens parser instead of reimplementing normalizeDebt, loading src/data/parse.ts in memory through the Lens checkout's own Vite server and calling buildWorkspace per case. It compares acceptance, rejection path and canonical projection against the corpus and asserts the observed Lens projection equals the Kyro canonical projection. REVIEW FIX: the corpus now carries six additional legacy-vocabulary vectors, so the gate covers the whole observable Lens surface rather than the canonical keys alone — non-string severity/source/resolution/disposition, an unmapped severity with and without an explicit priority, and a valid severity that supplies the absent priority.

tasks.title: Certify contract and projected-runtime parity
tasks.description: Wire the focused contract, fixture, Doctor, mutation, and projected-runtime checks into the appropriate aggregate gates and prove existing remediation, debt, checkpoint, build, and packaging behavior remains intact.
tasks.context: Apply original-incident-gate and shared-debt-vectors. Source-only PASS is insufficient: the projected runtime must execute the same classification cases. The Lens checkout-dependent command may remain an explicit cross-repository gate in this sprint, but its successful execution must be recorded as task evidence. Do not weaken or delete existing v1/v2 remediation tests to fit the new contract.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build, the focused debt contract and fixture checks, Doctor v4 checks, debt checks, verification-state checks, and the aggregate npm run check pass.
The projected runtime executes the faithful classification corpus and produces the same outcomes as source dist.
The Lens conformance command passes against the configured Lens checkout and its mutation proof demonstrates binding.
Existing v1/v2 remediation, recertification, checkpoint integrity, and package dry-run checks retain their previous passing behavior.
Doctor and analyze for this scope contain no CRITICAL or HIGH findings; future-sprint scenario coverage remains explicit rather than fabricated.

evidence.summary: Wired the contract into the aggregate and projected-runtime gates. check:debt-contract and check:debt-contract-fixture run inside npm run check; check-debt-contract.mjs honours KYRO_DIST_UNDER_TEST, and check-cli-bundle-assets drives the same faithful corpus through the isolated projected runtime, asserting the full result rather than a bare exit code. REVIEW FIX: the projected-runtime coverage assertion was re-pinned to the extended corpus (204 assertions over 14 cases), so a runtime that classified only the original eight cases would fail the gate instead of passing it. Existing v1/v2 remediation, recertification, checkpoint integrity and packaging suites were re-run unchanged: none were weakened or deleted to fit the new contract.
